speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry whether JTC's mandatory solar deployment scheme can be expanded to all tenants, with JTC offering (i) incentives for tenants with short remaining leases to make up for the inconvenience and (ii) to own solar installations and lease these to tenants with the shortest remaining leases.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry whether there are any plans to develop a set of landlord-to-tenant solar energy purchasing guidelines and to promote such arrangements, given the mutual benefits of lower-cost rooftop solar energy.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For commercial and industrial buildings which deploy solar power on a solar leasing model, the solar developers typically sell the solar energy captured to building owners who would use it to offset the electricity consumption in common areas.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For instances where the solar installation is owned by building owners, the solar energy is typically used for common areas by the owners.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Electricity charges and savings are negotiated between the landlords and tenants as part of their overall tenancy agreements.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: With this in view, it is not appropriate for us to provide guidelines on solar savings alone.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Nevertheless, landlords can consider taking reference from practices established by JTC Corporation (JTC) aimed to encourage solar adoption.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: JTC adopts a two-pronged approach to encourage solar adoption amongst their lessees.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: This was initially started to solarise JTC's own buildings.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: SolarRoof was expanded in 2020 to other buildings to make solar adoption more accessible for lessees, including those with shorter leases.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The first model available is through rooftop licensing, where lessees can lease their space to any solar vendor for solar panel installations in return for a rental fee.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The second model is solar leasing, where lessees allow vendors to install solar panels on their rooftops and they pay a discounted rate on the electricity generated which offsets their electricity consumption.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Lessees can adopt the two deployment schemes under the SolarRoof programme if they do not wish to own the solar panels themselves.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Just one supplementary question which is in relation to creating incentives to retrofit, for those that are not covered by the mandatory rule where there is a new tender or new construction, for existing facilities where there is no mandatory rule.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I think in some cases, there is an issue where the landlord is not incentivised to really do a solar deployment, which may be able to benefit the tenant.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I am wondering whether this is something that the Government can look at in terms of specifying guidelines whereby the benefits can be shared by the landlord and the tenant and there may be electricity generated that goes beyond what is needed for common areas.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Such guidelines may be able to incentivise both the landlord and the tenant to do a solar deployment in cases where it is not mandatory.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: So, is that something that we can look at?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Earlier, I cited JTC's mandatory solar deployment scheme.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: This includes JTC's vacant industrial land and buildings owned by JTC and its lessees.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to assure Mr Leon Perera that JTC's mandatory solar deployment scheme ensures that the lessees, which means the owner of the building, solarise their rooftops in line with the national efforts to increase our solar energy adoption.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The prerequisite for the mandatory solar deployment scheme is established by JTC in consultation with the solar vendors.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: These requirements are needed to ensure that both the lessee as well as the solar vendor have sufficient runway and skill to amortise the upfront fixed investments into the solar panel installation.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Having said that, I want to assure Mr Leon Perera that any lessee with shorter lease period of less than 15 years, or even smaller rooftop space of less than 800 square metres, they can still engage the solar vendor, including JTC's appointed solar vendor to participate in the SolarRoof Programme.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I also want to reassure him that JTC is currently seeking new solar vendors who are able to service shorter contract periods so that we can benefit the lessees and the tenant of shorter compact periods.
